knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to follow first-aid instructions and the SDS, seek medical help when indicated, and report through the incident pathway. Medical judgements are not made by the worker.
The lesson says to stop when unknown sharps or significant bodily fluids are found, and not to handle them without authorisation, training and equipment.
The instruction says to stop the task when encountering unknown sharps, significant bodily fluids, uncontrolled splashes or symptoms of chemical exposure.

practicalCriteria: Follows the authorised sequence and site procedures
Uses suitable tools, product instructions and contamination controls
Recognises and escalates unsafe or out-of-scope conditions
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 1: Stop the task on finding unknown sharps, significant bodily fluids, uncontrolled splashes or symptoms of chemical exposure.
Record of procedure step 3: Keep others away from the hazard where it is safe to do so, and secure the area as permitted.
Record of procedure step 6: Report the event promptly through the workplace incident pathway. Do not attempt an untrained clean-up.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Stop the task on finding unknown sharps, significant bodily fluids, uncontrolled splashes or symptoms of chemical exposure.
Stop work if procedure step 2 is not done: Leave any unknown sharp untouched. Do not handle sharps or biological material without the required authorisation, training and equipment.
Stop work if procedure step 3 is not done: Keep others away from the hazard where it is safe to do so, and secure the area as permitted.
